name: Brandenburg-Prussia

predecessors.text: the Hohenzollern Electorate of Brandenburg, the core of the realm and its seat at Berlin

predecessors.name: Duchy of Prussia
predecessors.text: the Duchy of Prussia, inherited by the Brandenburg Electors on Albert Frederick's death in 1618 and held as a fief of the Polish Crown until 1656/57

rulers.name: Frederick (Elector; crowned King in Prussia as Frederick I on 18 January 1701)

ledger.x: 1618: the Hohenzollern Electors of Brandenburg inherit the Duchy of Prussia and the two lands become Brandenburg-Prussia.
1631: Sweden fights its way into Brandenburg.
October 1648: Westphalia awards Farther Pomerania to Brandenburg, but 'the treaty did not decide the Swedish-Brandenburgian border in the Duchy of Pomerania' and Sweden had controlled it since 1630.
24 October 1648: Brandenburg-Prussia is compensated with the secularised bishoprics.
1648: the Swedish-Brandenburg fighting in the Mark ends with the Peace of Westphalia (signed 24 October 1648).
1653: the Treaty of Stettin fixes the Brandenburg-Swedish border in Pomerania. the Treaty of Stettin (1653) set the border with Swedish Pomerania
1657: the Treaty of Bromberg gives Brandenburg-Prussia Lauenburg-Bütow and Draheim (the Treaty of Wehlau-Bromberg also confirmed Brandenburg's sovereignty in Ducal Prussia, but not Ermland).
29 June 1679: at Saint-Germain Brandenburg keeps a strip of Pomerania.

July 1682: Brandenburg plants its colony on the Gold Coast. the Brandenburg African Company was founded on 7 March 1682 and an expedition in July began the fortress Großfriedrichsburg; a 16 May 1681 treaty with the chiefs had allowed a fort, and Fort Dorotheenschanze was agreed on 24 February 1684.
1686: Brandenburg renounces its Silesian claims in favour of the Habsburgs and receives the Silesian County of Schwiebus.
1694: Schwiebus goes back to the Habsburgs (the page: returned in 1694).
15 January 1701: the colony passes to the new kingdom.
18 January 1701: Frederick crowns himself King in Prussia and the realm becomes the Kingdom of Prussia.

wars.name: Thirty Years' War
wars.outcome: Brandenburg changed sides several times and was devastated by Swedish and Catholic forces; at Westphalia (24 October 1648) it received Farther Pomerania and the bishoprics of Halberstadt, Kammin and Minden, with succession rights to Magdeburg.

wars.name: Second Northern War (Brandenburg's part)
wars.outcome: Frederick William fought Sweden and Poland and changed sides in 1657: the Treaty of Königsberg (January 1656) took Ducal Prussia and Ermland as Swedish fiefs, Labiau (November 1656) gave full sovereignty, Wehlau-Bromberg (1657) confirmed it but not for…

wars.name: Jülich succession invasion
wars.outcome: Frederick William invaded Jülich-Berg and the affair ended with the Treaty of Kleve in October 1651; no border moved (the Great Elector page says his title to Cleves, Jülich and Ravensberg was 'definitely recognized' in 1666).

wars.name: Franco-Dutch War (Brandenburg's part)
wars.outcome: Brandenburg first allied with the Dutch Republic, made peace with France in the June 1673 Treaty of Vossem, then joined the imperial side in the Reichskrieg against France; no border moved.

wars.name: Scanian War (Brandenburg-Swedish War)
wars.outcome: Sweden invaded Brandenburg in 1674-1675 (Fehrbellin); Frederick William took Stettin (siege 1677) and most of Swedish Pomerania, and in the Treaty of Saint-Germain-en-Laye (29 June 1679) returned most of it, keeping the east bank of the Oder except Gollnow…

certainty.note: Thirty Years' War: the Swedish-held and ravaged parts of Brandenburg and Pomerania moved without a treaty line; the scattered Rhenish lands are drawn from the Cliopatria outline.
Borders fixed by treaty: Westphalia (1648), Stettin (1653), Bromberg (1657), Oliva (1660), Saint-Germain (1679).
